claims.text: Combining first-principles phonon-dispersion calculations with statistical modelling of force-constant fluctuations will predict low lattice thermal conductivity in HEAs more accurately than empirical or simplified models.
FeCoCrMnNi-type HEAs can form random, single-phase, homogeneously mixed structures exhibiting severe lattice distortion.
DFT-based phonon calculations combined with statistical force-constant distributions can be used to simulate phonon scattering in HEAs.
The relevant measurements can be performed at room temperature and extended to low temperatures.
Random atomic environments in HEAs produce local variations in force constants.
Severe lattice distortion in HEAs enhances phonon scattering.
Force-constant fluctuations attenuate acoustic phonons in FeCoCrMnNi-type HEAs.
Severe lattice distortion causes the force-constant fluctuations responsible for enhanced scattering.
Attenuation of heat-carrying phonons contributes to low lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy materials.
Explicitly modelling force-constant fluctuations will accurately capture acoustic-phonon attenuation.
Predicted phonon-dispersion curves and attenuation rates will correlate strongly with reduced lattice thermal conductivity.
The method will identify HEAs whose lattice thermal conductivities are significantly lower than values predicted by empirical mixing rules.
The proposed method will improve predictive accuracy against experimental benchmark data.
Current empirical mixing rules and simplified models do not fully account for random force-constant fluctuations in HEAs.
The predictive model is applicable only to single-phase, well-mixed HEAs.
The model's accuracy will degrade for multiphase or compositionally segregated alloys because its homogeneity assumptions no longer hold.
The exact magnitude of force-constant fluctuations and temperature-dependent scattering remains quantitatively uncertain.
Systematically varying elemental composition will modulate lattice distortion across the experimental HEA series.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant accuracy improvement over empirical models across the HEA series would falsify the proposed approach.
